item.title: CIA station in Saudi Arabia struck by suspected Iranian drone — report
item.description: An internal alert at the US State Department says the CIA building in Saudi Arabia sustained structural damage, according to a report.

item.title: US loses nearly $2 billion worth of military equipment in first 4 days of war on Iran
item.description: The main driving cost, according to data compiled by Anadolu, is the US AN/FPS-132 early warning radar system at Al Udeid Air Base in Qatar, valued at $1.1 billion.

item.title: Israeli-US war on Iran largest US military buildup in Middle East in decades: CENTCOM
item.description: US Central Command says 50,000 troops, 200 fighter jets and two aircraft carriers also take part in attacks, with nearly 2,000 targets struck across the country.

item.title: Palestinian activist's lawyers blast US deportation case as 'sham', vow to fight ruling
item.description: Mahmoud Khalil's legal team says the proceedings against him were fundamentally unfair and politically motivated, with a federal order temporarily blocking his deportation.

item.title: US troops told Iran war is 'God's plan' to trigger Armageddon, watchdog says
item.description: More than 200 complaints allege military commanders framed US strikes on Iran as part of a biblical prophecy, invoking the Book of Revelation and describing Trump as divinely 'anointed', according to the Military Religious Freedom Foundation.

item.title: ASEAN diplomats 'seriously concerned' over Middle East escalation, urge respect for UN Charter
item.description: Foreign ministers of the 11-member bloc call for immediate cessation of hostilities and avoiding actions that could further aggravate the situation in the region.

item.title: Nepal heads to crucial post-uprising election as main rivals battle seats outside capital
item.description: Six months after deadly anti-corruption protests toppled the government, nearly 19 million voters prepare to elect a new parliament in a tightly contested race stretching from Kathmandu to the Terai plains.

item.title: South Korea Navy chief suspended over alleged role in failed martial law bid
item.description: The move comes following a Defence Ministry committee review of allegations that Kang Dong-gil aided efforts to form a martial law command on the night of December 3 2024.

item.title: Myanmar junta starts rationing fuel for private vehicles, as Middle East crisis disrupt supply
item.description: Under a new 'even-odd' licensing scheme, even-numbered plates will only be allowed to drive on even dates, and odd-numbered plates on odd dates, according to an announcement.

item.title: Daily News Brief | 4 March
item.description: Suspected Iranian drone targets CIA station at US embassy in Saudi Arabia causing fire and damage. And, Turkish president criticises world powers for destabilising international order... listen for more
